title: Linear vector space
text: Define a linear vector space and list any three properties that its vectors must satisfy.
answer:
A vector space $V$ over a field $F$ is a set equipped with vector addition and scalar multiplication, satisfying the vector-space axioms.

Closure means $u+v\in V$ and $au\in V$ for $u,v\in V$ and $a\in F$.

Two of the requested three properties are commutativity, $u+v=v+u$, and associativity, $(u+v)+w=u+(v+w)$.

The third is the additive identity: a zero vector $0\in V$ exists such that $v+0=v$ for every $v\in V$.

steps.prompt: First, what two operations must the space support?
steps.explanation: These are the two defining operations.

steps.prompt: What must happen when two allowed vectors are added?
options: The sum stays in the space
steps.explanation: This is closure under addition.

steps.prompt: Which equation states commutativity?
steps.explanation: Swapping summands does not change the result.

steps.prompt: Which gives the additive identity property?
steps.explanation: The zero vector leaves every vector unchanged.

title: What makes a space Hilbert?
text: What is a Hilbert space? Mention the role of the scalar product in defining a Hilbert space.
answer:
A Hilbert space is a vector space with an inner product, complete under its induced norm $\|v\|=\sqrt{\langle v|v\rangle}$.

The scalar product defines overlaps, lengths, and the distance used for completeness.

steps.prompt: What structure measures overlap?
steps.explanation: The scalar product pairs two vectors.

steps.prompt: What is still required after specifying an inner product?
steps.explanation: No Cauchy limits may be missing.

title: Scalar product
text: Define the scalar product of two state vectors | ψ ⟩ and | ϕ ⟩ .
answer:
The scalar product $\langle\phi|\psi\rangle$ is the complex number obtained by pairing the bra of $|\phi\rangle$ with $|\psi\rangle$.

In an orthonormal basis, $\langle\phi|\psi\rangle=\sum_n\phi_n^*\psi_n$; it is linear in the second slot, conjugate-symmetric, and positive on a nonzero vector paired with itself.

steps.prompt: Which coefficients are conjugated?
steps.explanation: Use the bra of the first vector.

steps.prompt: What kind of object is the result?
steps.explanation: An overlap is a number.

title: Turn a ket into a bra
text: Write the bra corresponding to the ket |ψ> = a |Φ₁> + b |Φ₂>
answer:
Taking the Hermitian adjoint changes each ket into a bra and complex-conjugates its scalar coefficient: $(a|\Phi_1\rangle)^\dagger=a^*\langle\Phi_1|$.

Therefore $\langle\psi|=a^*\langle\Phi_1|+b^*\langle\Phi_2|$.

steps.prompt: First, what happens to a and b?
steps.explanation: The bra is conjugate-linear in the ket coefficients.

steps.prompt: Which is the resulting bra?
steps.explanation: Convert kets to bras and conjugate the scalars.

title: Hermitian adjoint
text:
Define the Hermitian adjoint Â† of a linear operator Â in terms of inner products.
State the condition under which an operator is strictly Hermitian.
answer:
The adjoint is defined by $\langle u|Av\rangle=\langle A^\dagger u|v\rangle$.

In finite dimensions, an operator is Hermitian when $A=A^\dagger$.
For an unbounded self-adjoint operator, its domain must also equal the adjoint domain.

steps.prompt: Which identity defines the adjoint?
steps.explanation: Move A to the other slot as its adjoint.

steps.prompt: For a finite matrix, when is it Hermitian?
steps.explanation: Equality with its adjoint is the criterion.

title: Commutator product rules
text: Using basic commutation relation [x, p] = iℏ evaluate [x, p²] and [x², p]
answer:
Use the product rules $[A,BC]=[A,B]C+B[A,C]$ and $[AB,C]=A[B,C]+[A,C]B$, with $[x,p]=i\hbar I$.

Then $[x,p^2]=[x,p]p+p[x,p]=i\hbar p+pi\hbar=2i\hbar p$.

Likewise $[x^2,p]=x[x,p]+[x,p]x=xi\hbar+i\hbar x=2i\hbar x$.

steps.explanation: Expand using the product rule.

steps.explanation: Each of the two terms equals iℏp.

steps.prompt: What is $[x^2,p]$?
steps.explanation: Expand x² as a product.

text: What is meant by a function f(Â) of an operator?

For a polynomial $f(t)=\sum_{n=0}^N c_nt^n$, define $f(A)=\sum_{n=0}^N c_nA^n$, with $A^0=I$.
Convergent power series and suitable spectral constructions extend this definition.

title: Common eigenvectors
text: What can be said about simultaneous eigenvectors of commuting operators?
answer:
Commuting Hermitian operators in a finite-dimensional space can be simultaneously diagonalized: a common orthonormal eigenbasis can be chosen.

If an eigenvalue of one operator is degenerate, diagonalize the other within that eigenspace.

steps.prompt: Under the finite Hermitian assumptions, commuting operators admit…
steps.explanation: Commutation preserves eigenspaces.

steps.prompt: What if an eigenspace is degenerate?
options: Diagonalize the other operator inside it
Choose any vector and it always works
steps.explanation: A suitable shared basis can be chosen.

verify: The common-eigenbasis statement needs assumptions such as finite-dimensional Hermitian operators; commutation alone is insufficient for arbitrary operators.

title: Degenerate eigenvalues
answer:
An eigenvalue is degenerate when two or more linearly independent eigenvectors have that same eigenvalue.
Its degeneracy is the dimension of the eigenspace.

steps.prompt: What must distinct eigenvectors share for degeneracy?

title: Position wave function
text: What is the position-space wave function of a state | ψ ⟩ ?
answer:
The position-space wave function is $\psi(x)=\langle x|\psi\rangle$.
For a normalized state, $|\psi(x)|^2dx$ is the probability of finding the particle in a small interval of width $dx$ around $x$.

title: Connecting two representations
text: How are position and momentum wave functions connected?
answer:
The position and momentum wave functions form a Fourier transform pair: $\phi(p)=\frac1{\sqrt{2\pi\hbar}}\int_{-\infty}^{\infty}e^{-ipx/\hbar}\psi(x)\,dx$.

The inverse is $\psi(x)=\frac1{\sqrt{2\pi\hbar}}\int_{-\infty}^{\infty}e^{ipx/\hbar}\phi(p)\,dp$.

steps.prompt: Which transformation connects the two?
steps.explanation: It changes the continuous basis.

steps.prompt: What is the forward phase sign?
steps.explanation: The inverse uses the conjugate phase.
